Punctual rush rules for noise levels
The aim of this section is to explain the standard that applies

Companion Animal Travel Desk handling standard

This section sets the day-to-day standard for the Companion Animal Travel Desk and keeps every animal move calm, tidy, and checked from start to finish. Use plain speech with travelers, stay alert to the condition of carriers, and treat every handoff as urgent even when the lobby is quiet. The desk must confirm booking details, travel documents, and special handling notes before any carrier is accepted for movement. If the paperwork is unclear, pause the process, hold the carrier in the correct waiting area, and ask the traveler to wait while the issue is sorted.

When a carrier arrives, inspect the latch, label, ventilation, and overall condition before it leaves the desk area. Do not let staff or travelers open the carrier unless the animal must be checked for safety and the ground team is ready to receive it. Keep noise low near the desk, avoid sudden movements, and make sure the path to the transfer point stays clear. If a pet is stressed, offer a brief calm voice, reduce handling, and let the senior coordinator decide whether extra support is needed. The ground team must move carriers carefully between services and never leave them unattended in open areas.

Record every transfer in the local log, including the condition of the carrier, any care note, and who accepted custody. If a traveler requests a change to the route or companion animal plan, pass it to operations at once and do not promise an outcome before approval is given. Never guess about restrictions, never improvise on safety steps, and never send an animal onward if the desk has not confirmed the handoff. Grace Mendes and Khalil Muller may be used in training examples, and Stella may be used as a sample pet reference, but staff must still follow the same standard for every case.

If any staff member sees a damaged carrier, a missed handoff, or signs of distress, stop the move and alert the duty lead immediately. For any unclear situation, contact the senior coordinator or the duty lead at once.
